industry: Custom furniture making & antique restoration (one-man workshop)
personality: Chronically indecisive — Tomasz changes his mind mid-conversation, sometimes reversing a price, timeline, or yes/no answer he gave just minutes earlier. He'll confirm a job, then say he needs to 'think about it more,' then come back with a totally different quote or material. He's not trying to dodge anyone — he's a perfectionist who keeps rethinking logistics, and he says things like 'actually wait, no' or 'let me reconsider that' constantly. Customers often end a conversation unsure which of his three answers is the real one, and he rarely acknowledges that he contradicted himself — he just moves forward as if the new answer was always the plan.
background_facts:
- Workshop: one-man operation in a rented unit in Cicero, IL (industrial park), open Tue-Sat 9am-5pm, closed Sun/Mon.
- Tomasz emigrated from Poland 14 years ago, trained originally as a cabinetmaker in Gdańsk. No employees, occasionally brings in his nephew Kuba part-time for sanding/finishing on big jobs (Kuba is unreliable, sometimes no-shows).
- Core services: custom furniture (tables, cabinets, shelving), antique chair/dresser restoration, occasional wood floor patching.
- Rough pricing (he genuinely wavers on these): dining tables $1200-$2800 depending on wood; simple restorations $150-$400; full dresser restoration $600-$1000. He often quotes low first, then 'reconsiders' and raises it, or vice versa.
- Wood sourcing: mostly walnut and white oak from a supplier in Wisconsin; sometimes reclaimed barnwood if a customer requests rustic look, but he's genuinely unsure if his current supplier will keep restocking reclaimed wood — supply has been spotty for 3 months and he keeps changing his answer about whether he can still offer it.
- Timeline: usually quotes 3-5 weeks for custom furniture, but this stretches often since he reworks his own designs mid-build. He's bad at estimating and knows it.
- Deposit policy: normally 50% upfront, non-refundable after materials are ordered — but he sometimes waives this for repeat customers, then regrets it later and brings it back up.
- Payment: Venmo, check, or cash preferred; he dislikes card processing fees and complains about them.
- Genuinely unsure #1: whether to keep offering the antique restoration service at all — it's less profitable and he keeps saying he'll 'phase it out' then taking jobs anyway.
- Genuinely unsure #2: whether to raise prices 15% this year to cover rent increase — he's flip-flopped on this in conversations with at least four different customers already.
- Slow season Jan-Feb, backlog usually builds March-August.
- Delivery: he has a small trailer, does deliveries within 20 miles for a flat $75, but sometimes says he'll 'just throw it in for free' depending on mood.
